release.html:
Full rewrite for SPT 4.1.1. SPT's server moved from Node.js/TypeScript to C#/.NET in the 4.x line, so old JS-based mods (including earlier Limitless releases) can't load on it anymore — this is a ground-up rewrite, not a patch.

What's new

  • Rewritten in C# against the SPT 4.1.1 server API
  • Fixed a bug in the original where "global limits" mutated barter_scheme (an item's price) instead of the item's actual stock fields — global limits no longer affect price
  • Config simplified to PersonalLimits / GlobalLimits, each with Unlimited (bool) and Multiplier (only used when Unlimited is false; 1 = no change)
  • Registers with SPT 4.1's Server Information Center "Configs" page, so settings can be viewed and edited live from the browser without restarting the server

Installation

Extract the zip at the root of your SPT install — files land in SPT_Runtime/user/mods/Limitless/.

If you're still on SPT 3.11.x, use the 3.11-0.1.1 release instead.

What's Changed

Three fixes for #10 reported by @DigitalBurns:

1. Container Loot Hang Fixed

Bots getting stuck in "Complete" looting state for 60s. Added action-level timeout (70s) in LootingLayer as a safety net when internal signals are lost, plus fixed a missing _target reset in LootCorpseLogic.

2. Raiders/Rogues No Longer Receive Questing Objectives

Raiders (brain name "PMC", but WildSpawnType.pmcBot) and Rogues were falling through the PMC/Scav role guards in QuestingLayer and getting stuck on bad waypoints — especially on Woods. Added explicit role allowlist: only actual PMCs and Scavs get questing now.

3. Backwards Walking Fixed

All GoToPoint() calls were passing false for the lookToMovingDirection parameter, leaving EFT's locomotion with no facing constraint. Changed to true across all movement calls. This is a one-time path hint (not the per-frame override removed in v1.2.0), so enemy detection remains unaffected.

Stats

  • Build: 0 errors, 0 warnings
  • Tests: 220 passing (29 new)
  • Files changed: 13

Installation

Extract the archive directly into your SPT root folder (where SPT.Server.exe is located).

Requires: SPT 4.0.12 + BigBrain 1.4.x

Thanks

  • @DigitalBurns — for detailed bug reports with BotDebug screenshots and BepInEx logs on both #9 and #10. Two releases worth of fixes came from your reports!
  • Guntero, simjounhax, alecontt — for reporting questing stuck behavior on SPT Forge

release.html:
What's Changed

This release applies fixes from a comprehensive code review and decomposes the InventoryService god class into focused, single-responsibility services. No user-facing behavior changes - all improvements are internal quality, security, and performance.

Architecture

  • InventoryService decomposed: 2,500+ line god class split into 4 focused services (AmmoCaptureStrategy, GridCaptureStrategy, InsuranceFilter, ItemSerializer) and 2 utilities (SessionIdValidator, GuiDrawingHelper). Net reduction: ~1,960 lines.

Security Fixes

  • Unsafe JSON deserialization: Added TypeNameHandling.None to all JsonConvert.DeserializeObject calls, preventing arbitrary type instantiation from malicious JSON
  • Recursion bomb prevention: Added depth limit (5 levels) and visited-object set to InsuranceFilter.ExtractInsuredIdsFromObject()
  • Session ID max length: Enforced 128-character maximum to prevent oversized IDs in file paths

Bug Fixes

  • ProtectionIndicator TOCTOU race: Replaced File.Exists() + read with try-catch on GetLastWriteTimeUtc()
  • SnapshotSoundPlayer init loop: Fixed infinite retry when initialization throws by moving flag to finally block
  • LoadoutProfiles underscore parsing: Fixed profile name extraction for session IDs containing underscores

Performance

  • Cached JsonSerializerOptions in SnapshotRestorer (eliminates per-call metadata rebuilds)
  • Session ID cached for 30 seconds in ProfileService (no repeated JSON parsing)
  • ProtectionIndicator file metadata cached (skip redundant re-reads)
  • ValueCalculator dictionary lookup replacing if-chain

Testing

  • 48/48 tests pass (10 serialization + 38 restoration algorithm)
  • In-game verified: 2 raids, both deaths restored correctly (42 items)
  • No snapshot format changes; fully backwards compatible

Compatibility

  • SPT 4.0.x (tested on 4.0.11)

release.html:
Dev Tools 1.8.0

1.0.0 was godmode and an ESP. This turns it into a full test bench: spawn what you want, freeze it,
shoot it where you choose, and read exactly what happened.

Everything is off by default, client-side, and lives under F12. Nothing is networked — no server mod,
no packets — but it does drive the raid when you ask it to, and bots belong to the host, so on a co-op
server bot spawning, freezing and killing act for everyone in the raid.

Shooting and damage

  • Limb Aim Assist — steer your shots onto a chosen body part (head, thorax, stomach, either arm or
    leg) of the bot nearest your crosshair. Only the shot direction changes; the round keeps its real
    ballistics, so armor zones, penetration and pellet spread all behave. Your view never moves. An
    Aim FOV cone decides what counts as the target, and Trigger picks between steering every
    shot or only shots fired while aiming down sights.
  • Hit Log — what each hit actually did: body part, the damage that reached flesh, whether the round
    beat the armor (with its penetration value) or was stopped, plus armor damage, target and range.
    Penetrating and blocked hits are coloured differently.

Spawning

  • Spawn any bot at your crosshair — pick a type, difficulty and count, press a key. The type list
    is read from the running game, so modded factions appear automatically without this mod knowing they
    exist. Bots come through the game's own spawn pipeline, so they get real loadouts, brains and
    grouping, and they are placed on walkable ground at your aim point.
  • Spawn any item — a searchable catalogue of every item the client knows about, modded items
    included. Filter by category, click to have it placed in your inventory.

Bots

  • Bots Ignore Me — drop off every bot's target list, including bots already hunting you. They carry
    on fighting each other.
  • Freeze Bots — they stop thinking, moving and shooting where they stand. Toggling off resumes
    them; nothing is reset.
  • Kill All Bots — clear the map between tests.
  • Bot Loadout Inspector — aim at a bot and read its whole generated kit: weapons with their fitted
    mods, armor, rig, helmet, stacks, and condition. For checking a loadout config came out the way you
    wrote it, without killing the bot and looting the body. Positionable, so it need not sit on your
    minimap.

Getting around and seeing

  • Freecam — fly anywhere, through anything. It flies you rather than a detached camera, so the
    view, mouse look and HUD behave normally; toggling off returns you to where you took off from.
  • Waypoints — save a spot and teleport back to it later. Survives a restart.
  • ESP gains a text-only Labels style and a Show Distance toggle.

World

  • Time Of Day moves the raid clock and the sun with it, for optics, night vision and glare work.

commit.message: One sensitivity across every movement state, free look included

release.html:
One mouse sensitivity, everywhere. The game quietly scales your look speed down while you sprint, jump, crouch, go prone or sit in the transitions between poses, and drains it further with your stamina mid-sprint. This removes all of it: turning at a dead sprint feels exactly like turning while standing.

Jumping needed two extra fixes, because mid-air the game does not just cut your sensitivity - it eases your body toward where you are looking instead of taking the turn outright, and it caps how far any single frame is allowed to rotate, which clipped fast flicks while slow drags felt fine. Both are corrected: an airborne flick lands the frame you make it.

Free look rides your sensitivity too, stepped up 3x, instead of the fixed speed the engine hardwires.

Deliberately untouched: gear. Armor still slows your turns, scopes keep their aim sensitivity, and weight still costs you jump height and takeoff speed. Do not run it alongside Sprint Sensitivity Fixer - this covers everything that mod does.

What's fixed

  • Critical: server could crash on startup, and profiles carrying a radio could be marked invalid.
    The mod's item-registration priority (TypePriority) was set too late in the load order, so on

commit.message: Document the 4.1 move in the README and changelog

release.html:
⚠️ This release is for SPT 4.1.x only

SPT 4.1 checks which server version a mod was built against and refuses to load mismatched mods, so this build will not run on SPT 4.0. If you're still on 4.0, stay on v4.4.0.

📁 The install folder changed

SPT 4.1 renamed its server folder from SPT/ to SPT_Runtime/. Extract the zip into your game root — the folder that contains SPT_Runtime/ — and the mod lands in SPT_Runtime\user\mods\CNN-Containers. Delete the old copy out of SPT\user\mods\CNN-Containers so you don't leave a stale build behind.

✅ Your containers and config are safe

This is an SPT compatibility release, not a rework. Item IDs, grid sizes, trader offers and prices are all unchanged, and your existing config/config.jsonc carries over as-is. Nothing needs emptying before you update — unlike v4.4.0, there is no change to how any container stores its contents.

Changed

  • Rebuilt for SPT 4.1.x on .NET 10, and migrated to 4.1's mod API — the new metadata interface, the async load lifecycle with shutdown cancellation support, and direct injection of the database tables now that the old database service is gone.
  • Containers register earlier in server startup. SPT 4.1 loads the database before anything else runs and asks mods that add their own items and trader offers to register at that point, so the containers and their trader assorts now exist before any profile is loaded.
  • Cloned items carry their own internal name — the Gear Box now identifies itself as item_container_gearbox instead of inheriting the name of the pouch it's cloned from. Cosmetic: it shows in logs and debugging tools, not in game.

Fixed

  • The mod reports its correct version in the server console. v4.4.0 announced itself as 4.3.0 because of a stale hardcoded string; the version is now read from the assembly, so it can't drift away from the release again.

Notes

  • The Mod Case and Ruined Wooden Box still show pink/purple textures — their bundles were built for an older Unity version and need recompiling. They work fine, they just look wrong. Unchanged from previous releases.
  • After updating, open the SPT launcher's settings and click Clean Temp Files before launching.

commit.message: Name 4.0.13 in the release notes and widen the unzip wording

release.html:
Requires SPT 4.1.3 (specifically) - use v0.13.0 if you are still on SPT4.1.2.

Still on SPT 4.0.x? Use v0.12.7. That line is still supported on the SPT4.0.x branch - both versions get the same features.

Changes

This is the first full release since v0.13.0. It carries everything from the v0.13.1-pre1 plus new support for headless clients on SPT 4.1.3.

Headless clients can get their asset bundles on SPT 4.1.3

SPT 4.1.3 moved bundle downloading out of the game client and into the launcher. A headless never runs the launcher, so on 4.1.3 it cannot download bundles.

ModSync now fetches them itself on a headless, before the game loads them. Bundles are CRC-verified and cached, so this happens once.

**If your headless shares a machine with your server, this shouldn't be an issue as SPT still falls back to reading a bundle out of its mod folder when the cache misses. If using docker and headless is in the same stack you can use:

# headless service
volumes:
  - ../headless:/opt/tarkov
  - ../server/SPT_Runtime/user/mods:/opt/tarkov/SPT_Runtime/user/mods:ro

Nothing is copied and no extra disk is used. ModSync then sees that every bundle is already reachable and downloads nothing - a 7 GB modset goes from a ~50 minute first boot to about two minutes. Without the mount, ModSync downloads them, which works everywhere but is limited to roughly 2-3 MB/s by Unity's Mono HTTP stack. Either way you end up with a working headless.

Note

Bundle fetching is a stopgap. It exists because there is no headless image for SPT 4.1.3 yet.
Once an official one ships and handles bundles itself, this will be removed from ModSync.

The mod-folder mount shown above is not affected and will keep working - that is SPT's own
lookup behaviour, not something ModSync adds.

Also, its slow without the mount, painfully so, but it works. If you have a networked setup with gigs of bundles, go have a Fika break!

New: optional per syncPath

Set "optional": true and the client gets a working checkbox for that path in the F12 menu, starting in whatever state enabled gives it. Until now the only path a player could tick or untick was an opt-IN one ("enabled": false); this adds the other half, a mod that is synced by default but can still be refused. Unticking uninstalls what ModSync installed there.

Do not put it on the three catch-alls (../BepInEx/plugins, patchers, config) - they carry the mods your players need to connect, so one untick would strip the modset.

New: removing a mod from your config now removes it from clients

Delete a mod's files from the server and delete its syncPaths entry, and every client uninstalls its copy on the next sync, with the usual prompt. Previously the entry disappearing meant clients never heard about it again and kept the mod permanently.

ModSync records what it served in .modsync-served.json next to config.jsonc, and keeps offering a removed entry as empty until you re-add it or clear that file. Deleting the entry but keeping the files still does the opposite, by design: the entry is what carves a mod out of the catch-alls, so without it they sync it to everyone.

Fixed: renaming a syncPath no longer resets your players' F12 choices

Each client stored its toggles under the syncPath's name, so relabelling an entry made every player's setting for that mod revert to default and left a dead line in their config. Toggles are now stored under the path and merely displayed using the name. Each client carries its existing choices over on the first launch and tidies the old lines away; nobody has to do anything.

This mattered more once optional existed: a reset re-ticks an opt-out path, which would have silently reinstalled a mod the player had refused.

Upgrade notes

Unzip into your game/server root as usual - clients update themselves via sync, no manual steps.

Your existing config.jsonc is untouched and behaves exactly as before; optional defaults to false.

If you already have an entry you expected players to be able to untick, it needs "optional": true adding. An "enabled": true path has never been shown in the F12 menu, and still isn't without that option.

Testing status

The four items carried over from v0.13.1-pre1 were tested on the 4.0 line through the v0.12.7 pre-releases, on live servers with headless and player clients, before being ported here unchanged.

Bundle acquisition is new in this release. It was tested on a live SPT 4.1.3 stack with a 1214-bundle / 7 GB modset, both ways: with the mount present (every bundle resolved from the mod folder, nothing downloaded) and with bundles deliberately hidden from it (fetched, CRC-verified and cached). Both test suites are green in CI.

Docs

  • syncPaths options - all eight, including optional
  • Retiring a mod - how removal reaches clients, and the keep-the-files trap

commit.message: Bump to 0.13.2 and write the release notes

release.html:
Requires SPT 4.1.3 (specifically) - use v0.13.0 if you are still on SPT4.1.2.

Still on SPT 4.0.x? Use v0.12.7. That line is still supported on the SPT4.0.x branch - both versions get the same features.

Changes

This is the first full release since v0.13.0. It carries everything from the v0.13.1-pre1 plus new support for headless clients on SPT 4.1.3.

Headless clients can get their asset bundles on SPT 4.1.3

SPT 4.1.3 moved bundle downloading out of the game client and into the launcher. A headless never runs the launcher, so on 4.1.3 it cannot download bundles.

ModSync now fetches them itself on a headless, before the game loads them. Bundles are CRC-verified and cached, so this happens once.

**If your headless shares a machine with your server, this shouldn't be an issue as SPT still falls back to reading a bundle out of its mod folder when the cache misses. If using docker and headless is in the same stack you can use:

# headless service
volumes:
  - ../headless:/opt/tarkov
  - ../server/SPT_Runtime/user/mods:/opt/tarkov/SPT_Runtime/user/mods:ro

Nothing is copied and no extra disk is used. ModSync then sees that every bundle is already reachable and downloads nothing - a 7 GB modset goes from a ~50 minute first boot to about two minutes. Without the mount, ModSync downloads them, which works everywhere but is limited to roughly 2-3 MB/s by Unity's Mono HTTP stack. Either way you end up with a working headless.

Note

Bundle fetching is a stopgap. It exists because there is no headless image for SPT 4.1.3 yet.
Once an official one ships and handles bundles itself, this will be removed from ModSync.

The mod-folder mount shown above is not affected and will keep working - that is SPT's own
lookup behaviour, not something ModSync adds.

Also, its slow without the mount, painfully so, but it works. If you have a networked setup with gigs of bundles, go have a Fika break!

New: optional per syncPath

Set "optional": true and the client gets a working checkbox for that path in the F12 menu, starting in whatever state enabled gives it. Until now the only path a player could tick or untick was an opt-IN one ("enabled": false); this adds the other half, a mod that is synced by default but can still be refused. Unticking uninstalls what ModSync installed there.

Do not put it on the three catch-alls (../BepInEx/plugins, patchers, config) - they carry the mods your players need to connect, so one untick would strip the modset.

New: removing a mod from your config now removes it from clients

Delete a mod's files from the server and delete its syncPaths entry, and every client uninstalls its copy on the next sync, with the usual prompt. Previously the entry disappearing meant clients never heard about it again and kept the mod permanently.

ModSync records what it served in .modsync-served.json next to config.jsonc, and keeps offering a removed entry as empty until you re-add it or clear that file. Deleting the entry but keeping the files still does the opposite, by design: the entry is what carves a mod out of the catch-alls, so without it they sync it to everyone.

Fixed: renaming a syncPath no longer resets your players' F12 choices

Each client stored its toggles under the syncPath's name, so relabelling an entry made every player's setting for that mod revert to default and left a dead line in their config. Toggles are now stored under the path and merely displayed using the name. Each client carries its existing choices over on the first launch and tidies the old lines away; nobody has to do anything.

This mattered more once optional existed: a reset re-ticks an opt-out path, which would have silently reinstalled a mod the player had refused.

Upgrade notes

Unzip into your game/server root as usual - clients update themselves via sync, no manual steps.

Your existing config.jsonc is untouched and behaves exactly as before; optional defaults to false.

If you already have an entry you expected players to be able to untick, it needs "optional": true adding. An "enabled": true path has never been shown in the F12 menu, and still isn't without that option.

Testing status

The four items carried over from v0.13.1-pre1 were tested on the 4.0 line through the v0.12.7 pre-releases, on live servers with headless and player clients, before being ported here unchanged.

Bundle acquisition is new in this release. It was tested on a live SPT 4.1.3 stack with a 1214-bundle / 7 GB modset, both ways: with the mount present (every bundle resolved from the mod folder, nothing downloaded) and with bundles deliberately hidden from it (fetched, CRC-verified and cached). Both test suites are green in CI.

  • Usage Examples - worked config.jsonc setups, from minimal to a real server

Full Changelog: v0.13.0...v0.13.2

⚠️ This release is for SPT 4.1.x only

SPT 4.1 checks which server version a mod was built against and refuses to load mismatched mods, so this build will not run on SPT 4.0. If you're still on 4.0, stay on v2.0.0.

📁 The install folder changed

SPT 4.1 renamed its server folder from SPT/ to SPT_Runtime/. Extract the zip into your game root — the folder that contains SPT_Runtime/ — and the mod lands in SPT_Runtime\user\mods\SouthernHemisphereSeasons. If you're upgrading from 4.0, delete the old copy out of SPT\user\mods\ so you don't leave a stale build behind.

Fixed

  • The hourly season recheck now actually runs hourly. It was comparing a value measured in seconds against a threshold written in milliseconds, so after the first check it only re-evaluated the season roughly every 41 days instead of every hour. On a server that stays up across a season boundary — start of a month, say — the season now changes over on time instead of waiting for a restart. Restarting the server always applied the correct season, so this only ever affected long uptimes.

Changed

  • Rebuilt for SPT 4.1.x on .NET 10.
  • Migrated to 4.1's mod API: the new metadata interface, the async load/update lifecycle with shutdown cancellation support, and direct config injection now that the old config server is gone.

Added

  • Unit tests covering the season calendar month by month, the forceSeason override and its out-of-range handling, and the season display names. These run automatically on every change, so a future SPT update that shifts the season values gets caught at build time rather than showing the wrong season in game.

Notes

  • Your config carries over unchanged. config/config.jsonc keeps the same three options with the same meanings — no edits needed when upgrading.
  • Season values for forceSeason are unchanged: 0 Summer, 1 Autumn, 2 Winter, 3 Spring, 4 Late Autumn, 5 Early Spring, null auto-detect.

release.html:
New

  • S8 CalmRagfairServer — vanilla forces a blocking, compacting full GC every time enough flea offers expire, a recurring multi-hundred-ms-to-multi-second stall. This runs the exact same expiry sequence minus the forced collect. In a measured session it skipped 54 forced GCs and the worst frame-pause dropped from ~8s (mod off) to ~1.7s.
  • S9 FastCompressionHttpListener — responses compressed at zlib Fastest instead of vanilla's slowest SmallestSize: several-fold less CPU for a few percent more bytes that only cross localhost/LAN. Output is byte-compatible.
  • S10 ThreadSafeCaches — serializes access to three SPT caches (handbook prices, item base classes, item blacklists) that vanilla writes at runtime while parallel ragfair tasks read them. Prevents an intermittent concurrent-collection crash.
  • S7 FastHttpResponseUtil — replaces five regex passes per response with one zero-allocation scan. Identical output.

Removed

  • The log-filtering pair (S3/C4) — dropped close to nothing on default setups and made other mods' bug reports worse. The mod is now server-only! No BepInEx plugin ships, which also clears the client/server GUID-mismatch warning in check-mods.

  • Upgrading from 1.2.x? Delete the old BepInEx/plugins/CompoundingPerf.Client folder.

v3.4.1 — Bug fixes

Two fixes for issues introduced by the 3.4.0 visual overhaul, both reported
from real use.

  • Closing a popup no longer opens another one. Clicking the X on the
    Stats window could trigger the Local Mods button sitting underneath it,
    leaving you with a second window to dismiss before getting back to the app.
    The popup was closing on mouse-down, which handed the mouse-up to
    whatever was behind it.

  • Change notes no longer cut off their last lines. A changelog longer than
    the popup but shorter than about 24 lines would simply stop partway, with no
    scrollbar and no response to the mouse wheel — the remaining lines were
    rendered below the visible area with no way to reach them. Scrolling now
    starts as soon as the content actually overflows.

Both fixes are on the shared components, so they apply to every popup and
every button in the app rather than just the two cases that surfaced them.

release.html:
Welcome Messages

This mod replaces the Beta warning message with a custom welcome message pulled from a collection of messages, each with a title and description. A new message is chosen at random every time the server starts, giving your SPT experience a little personality.

Features

  • Replaces the default Beta warning message on server start
  • 50+ messages (title + description pairs)
  • Messages loaded from appsettings.json
  • Random message chosen each server launch

Installation

  1. Download the mod and extract the folder.
  2. Move kitteh-welcome-messages into your mods directory: <YOUR SPT INSTALL>/SPT/user/mods
  3. Start your SPTarkov server, your new welcome message will appear.

Customization

  1. Open the appsettings.json file with a text editor located in kitteh-welcome-messages/config
  2. You edit, add, or remove entries as you see fit.

Uninstallation

  1. Stop the server if it's running.
  2. Delete the kitteh-welcome-messages folder from the mods directory.
  3. Restart the server, the default Beta warning returns.

Changelog

1.1.0

  • Complete rewrite of the per-raid hook. Previously used IOnBeforeEventRequestData, which is dead code in SPT and never fires. Mod was silently applying the same time every raid until server restart.
  • Now hooks MatchController.ConfigureOfflineRaid via Harmony postfix, which fires correctly on every raid start.
  • Replaced Console.WriteLine with ISptLogger (injected).
  • Replaced ServiceLocator with proper DI injection throughout.
  • Config reworked: dropped AllowIncrease and AllowDecrease in favor of a single Bias float using an odds-ratio model.
  • Config file is now resolved relative to the DLL — folder can be renamed freely.
  • Server console now logs map name, delta, and final raid time on each raid start.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.

Adds support for any night vision goggle without a mod update, and moves pose and mask tuning into the game.

Two downloads, one release. The major version encodes the SPT generation, and they are not interchangeable.

Download For
LennoxP90-COTI-3.0.0-spt4.1.7z SPT 4.1
LennoxP90-COTI-2.0.0-spt4.0.7z SPT 4.0

Installing: open the archive with 7-Zip and drag all of its contents into your SPT folder. Both halves are needed - the server registers the item, its slot on each device and the trader offer; the client does the rendering.

Borkel's Realistic NVGs is recommended but not required.

Added

  • Support for any night vision goggle, from a file. Each device is one JSON file in nvghostcompat/, so a new goggle needs no mod update. A file survives its host mod renumbering items, and declares which mod it needs so it is skipped cleanly when that mod is absent.
  • Automatic discovery. Any night vision item with no file gets one written for it, seeded from the closest device COTI already knows. A new goggle is mountable immediately, with a pose to correct rather than nothing at all.
  • Five more goggles supported: PNV-10T and PNV-57E, plus the Argus Chimera in all three variants, the ITT AN/PVS-5A and ACTinBlack DTNVS from C11 - True North.
  • In-game pose editor. A COTI Pose button on a goggle's inspect window opens position, rotation, scale and anchor-bone controls over a lit 3D preview, with a flip test to confirm the device travels with the tube. Publishing writes it to the server, so it is not lost on the next launch.
  • In-game mask editor. F12 -> Mask Editor opens a window that survives closing the menu, so the thermal circle can be moved, resized and softened in a raid while looking through the goggles. It saves itself as you adjust.
  • Three official addons, one per host mod, for goggles that come from another mod.

Changed

  • Image settings are global rather than per goggle, and all of them are on F12 under Advanced.
  • DTNVS and AN/PVS-31A support now ships as addons rather than inside the mod. If you use WTT-CAG or WTT-ContentBackport, download the matching addon below.

Addons

Optional. Each is a drag-over like the mod itself, and only needed if you have the host mod.

Addon Needs Adds
LennoxP90-COTI-addon-C11-TrueNorth-spt4.x.7z C11 - True North Argus Chimera (three variants), ITT AN/PVS-5A, ACTinBlack DTNVS
LennoxP90-COTI-addon-WTT-CAG-spt4.x.7z WTT - CAG ACTinBlack DTNVS, white and green phosphor
LennoxP90-COTI-addon-WTT-ContentBackport-spt4.x.7z WTT - ContentBackport AN/PVS-31A

Without the host mod they cost nothing and can be left in place. Anyone can write one; the format is documented in ADDONS.md.

Adds a custom item, so it cannot be cleanly removed from a profile once one has spawned or been bought.

Adds support for any night vision goggle without a mod update, and moves pose and mask tuning into the game.

Two downloads, one release. The major version encodes the SPT generation, and they are not interchangeable.

Download For
LennoxP90-COTI-3.0.0-spt4.1.7z SPT 4.1
LennoxP90-COTI-2.0.0-spt4.0.7z SPT 4.0

Installing: open the archive with 7-Zip and drag all of its contents into your SPT folder. Both halves are needed - the server registers the item, its slot on each device and the trader offer; the client does the rendering.

Borkel's Realistic NVGs is recommended but not required.

Added

  • Support for any night vision goggle, from a file. Each device is one JSON file in nvghostcompat/, so a new goggle needs no mod update. A file survives its host mod renumbering items, and declares which mod it needs so it is skipped cleanly when that mod is absent.
  • Automatic discovery. Any night vision item with no file gets one written for it, seeded from the closest device COTI already knows. A new goggle is mountable immediately, with a pose to correct rather than nothing at all.
  • Five more goggles supported: PNV-10T and PNV-57E, plus the Argus Chimera in all three variants, the ITT AN/PVS-5A and ACTinBlack DTNVS from C11 - True North.
  • In-game pose editor. A COTI Pose button on a goggle's inspect window opens position, rotation, scale and anchor-bone controls over a lit 3D preview, with a flip test to confirm the device travels with the tube. Publishing writes it to the server, so it is not lost on the next launch.
  • In-game mask editor. F12 -> Mask Editor opens a window that survives closing the menu, so the thermal circle can be moved, resized and softened in a raid while looking through the goggles. It saves itself as you adjust.
  • Three official addons, one per host mod, for goggles that come from another mod.

Changed

  • Image settings are global rather than per goggle, and all of them are on F12 under Advanced.
  • DTNVS and AN/PVS-31A support now ships as addons rather than inside the mod. If you use WTT-CAG or WTT-ContentBackport, download the matching addon below.

Addons

Optional. Each is a drag-over like the mod itself, and only needed if you have the host mod.

Addon Needs Adds
LennoxP90-COTI-addon-C11-TrueNorth-spt4.x.7z C11 - True North Argus Chimera (three variants), ITT AN/PVS-5A, ACTinBlack DTNVS
LennoxP90-COTI-addon-WTT-CAG-spt4.x.7z WTT - CAG ACTinBlack DTNVS, white and green phosphor
LennoxP90-COTI-addon-WTT-ContentBackport-spt4.x.7z WTT - ContentBackport AN/PVS-31A

Without the host mod they cost nothing and can be left in place. Anyone can write one; the format is documented in ADDONS.md.

Adds a custom item, so it cannot be cleanly removed from a profile once one has spawned or been bought.

SPT Mod Manager v0.5.3

A Vortex / Mod Organizer 2-style mod manager built specifically for SPT.

🇧🇷 Português: https://github.com/Nevek20/SPT_Mod_Manager/blob/main/README_pt-BR.md

⚠️ Before running

Windows will likely display a "Windows protected your PC" SmartScreen warning. This is expected for unsigned indie software and does not mean the application is malicious. Click More info then Run anyway.

Requirements

  • Windows
  • An existing SPT installation

Release 0.5.3

Small release, all from your comments. Every item here came from someone reporting something.

Mod search

  • Clicking a mod now opens that mod's page instead of the site's front page. The link had the right address on it all along; the click handler just ignored it.
  • New "Only what I don't have" checkbox. Hides mods you've already installed so you can see what's actually new to you. When it's on, the Manager also pulls a bigger page from the site, so there's still a list left after the hiding.
  • Both checkboxes now re-run the search when you click them. "Only compatible" used to need a second click on Search, which made it feel broken next to the other one.
  • The "Installed" badge updates right after installing, instead of waiting for you to search again.
  • Mods for a different SPT version are now labelled rather than just missing. Uncheck "Only compatible" and you'll see the whole catalogue, with a red mark on anything that doesn't fit your install and the version it targets in the tooltip. If you were hoping for a way to pick several SPT versions at once, this covers it: a mod marked ~4.1.0 already counts as compatible on 4.1.2, so the only ones hidden were those pinned to one exact version.

Errors

  • "Unexpected token '<'" is gone. That message appeared when the site answered with an error page instead of data, which the Manager then failed to read as JSON. It now tells you what actually came back, so a Cloudflare error, a site outage and a hotel Wi-Fi login page no longer all look like the same cryptic failure.

See the README for the complete feature list.

Installation

  1. Download SPT-Mod-Manager-0.5.3-win-x64.exe below.
  2. Run it (see the SmartScreen note above).
  3. Select your SPT installation folder on first launch.

Feedback

This is a personal project, so feedback, bug reports, and feature suggestions are always welcome.

NVIDIA Profile Inspector 3.0.2.1

Version 3.0.2.1 is the first major 3.x release and summarizes the final feature set introduced since 2.4.

Highlights

  • Modernized user interface with a redesigned window and title bar layout, updated About dialog, splash screen, status bar, and in-app notifications.
  • Built-in update functionality with GitHub release checking, Release and Pre-release channel selection, and a prepared in-place updater.
  • Greatly expanded settings browser with more flexible filters, improved metadata resolution, and better visibility of relevant values and changes.
  • Enhanced import/export workflows for .nip profiles and NVIDIA text formats, including Merge/Replace strategies and multi-file import.
  • Updated driver and settings data with support for newer NVIDIA settings, modern DLSS overrides, and additional current profile parameters.

User Interface and Usability

  • New modern visual style with multiple themes
  • Switchable display density for either a more compact or more spacious layout.
  • Windows backdrop support with matching options for Windows 10 and Windows 11
  • Improved status display with additional information such as driver version, profile count, setting count, and update status.
  • Update indicator directly in the UI.
  • Optional startup splash screen toggle.
  • Better visual feedback for actions such as Apply, Restore, Import, and profile selection.

Settings and Editing

  • New filtering logic for setting sources and value sources, replacing the older coarse-grained mode switching.
  • Optional Modified only filter to focus on changed or active entries.
  • Favorites support for frequently used settings.
  • Grouped and collapsible settings sections.
  • Search now also supports hexadecimal setting IDs.
  • Optional display of the setting ID directly in the setting name.
  • Optional display of the raw value alongside named common values.
  • Improved resolution of names, types, and value lists from multiple sources, with clearer prioritization of live driver-provided information.
  • Improved friendly names and value presentation for scanned and reference-based entries.
  • Proper support and validation for QWORD values.

Profiles, Import, and Export

  • .nip import now supports multiple files in a single operation.
  • Import can explicitly use either Merge or Replace.
  • Interactive imports now prompt for the appropriate import strategy when existing profiles are affected.
  • Improved export of all customized profiles.
  • Expanded and restored CLI workflows for import/export scenarios.
  • Additional import/export data such as FindFile application entries is now preserved and handled correctly.

Profiles and Applications

  • Improved modified profiles handling with a dedicated selector and more consistent refresh behavior.
  • More compact and clearer display of profile applications.
  • Better handling of long application entries and overflow.
  • FindFile support when adding applications.
  • Improved resolution of Steam and Epic launcher shortcuts to the actual game executable.
  • More robust behavior when deleting, restoring, and updating profiles and applications.

Driver Data and NVIDIA Settings

  • Updated NVAPI/DRS constants and reference data for newer driver generations.
  • Support for current DLSS, DLSS Ray Reconstruction, and DLSS Frame Generation-related override settings.
  • Support for additional current NVIDIA parameters such as RTX Dynamic Vibrance.
  • New or updated NVIDIA App Overlay flags and related overlay entries.
  • Extensive updates to CustomSettingNames.xml and Reference.xml for more accurate names, descriptions, and values.

KeepLockedCases v1.0.1

Fixes

  • Fixed arena weapon crates not giving cases — case-sensitive string comparison ("arena_weaponcrate" vs "Arena_weaponcrate_blue_open") prevented Unlocked Weapon Crate (Rare/Epic/Common) from being recognized, resulting in no loot and no bonus case
  • Added explicit ignore list for event containers (pumpkin, new year gifts, Twitch drops) so they pass through to SPT cleanly

Installation

Extract zip into your SPT installation directory (drag and drop).

Raid time is now real time. The in-raid clock starts at the host's system time
and runs 1:1 with it, raids no longer expire, and under Fika every player shares
the host's clock and sky.

Added

System time on the map screen. The raid setup screen showed the accelerated
Tarkov clock, whose seconds visibly drifted away from the system clock. It now
tracks DateTime.Now exactly, re-pinned every frame. The day/night slots keep
vanilla's layout, so picking one still selects a night raid.

Raids start at the current time and run at 1x. The raid begins at the host's
real system time to the second and advances at real speed instead of Tarkov's 7x.
Factory is left alone — it has two fixed times rather than a clock.

Raids are infinite. The session timer is extended rather than cleared, so it
never runs out and MIA never triggers. Extraction and transit countdowns are
untouched and still count down normally.

The in-raid timer shows a clock. The countdown is replaced with the current
raid time. Optional via the ShowClockInRaid config setting.

Host-authoritative sync under Fika. The host decides the time and every
client takes it, including the sky. Previously a client could load into darkness
inside a daytime raid: Fika syncs the clock but not the lighting, which recomputes
each frame from a separate reference the host never reaches. That reference is now
bound to the synced clock.

Verified in a two-machine Fika raid — both players in matching daylight, both
timers on the same raid clock. A client's displayed time sits a fixed ~1 minute
behind the host (its load time, frozen in at the moment it applies the host's
value); it stays constant and does not drift.

Optional trace logging. Off by default, under the Logging config section.

Fixed

  • The server mod failed to build once the client plugin was added, because the
    project was compiling the BepInEx sources into the server assembly.

Install

Extract into your SPT folder. Both halves are needed under Fika — the server mod
goes to user/mods/, the client plugin to BepInEx/plugins/, and every player
needs the client plugin.

Requires SPT ~4.1.0.

##Initial Release

Configurable death-loss rules for SPT. Overrides InRaidHelper so raid-end restoration
happens before the normal death penalty runs, instead of guessing at raid state from
profile files on disk.

Built for SPT 4.0.13.

Modes (config.jsonc, written next to the mod DLL on first load)

Mode Behaviour
Vanilla SPT default - lose all equipment on death
KeepEverything Nothing is lost on death
KeepGearOnly Keep the gear entered with (weapons, armor, pockets/rig/backpack as containers); contents of pockets/rig/backpack are always lost
KeepEntryItems Keep everything entered with, including pockets/rig/backpack contents; only items picked up during the raid are lost

SecuredContainer and Scabbard are always preserved, matching normal Tarkov rules,
independent of mode.

DefaultMode applies to any profile not listed in ProfileOverrides, which maps a profile
id (the filename, minus .json, under user/profiles/ on the server) to a rule for that
profile. Each rule's Maps is every SPT map id set to true/false: the rule's Mode only
takes effect on maps listed true there; a map left out or set to false falls back to
DefaultMode - same as an unlisted profile. Leave Maps out entirely (or empty) to apply the
rule on every map:

"DefaultMode": "Vanilla",
"ProfileOverrides": {
  "68abf1e2c9c2a1f4b5d6e7f8": {
    "Mode": "KeepEverything",
    "Maps": {
      "laboratory": true,
      "factory4_night": true,
      "shoreline": false
    }
  }
}

Map ids: bigmap, woods, factory4_day, factory4_night, interchange, rezervbase,
shoreline, laboratory, lighthouse, tarkovstreets, sandbox, sandbox_high. Keys are
matched case-insensitively.

PreserveFoundInRaid (default false): SPT clears the Found in Raid flag from everything in
the post-raid profile on death (InRaidHelper.RemoveFiRStatusFromItems), independent of what
this mod protects from deletion - so without this, an item kept via KeepEverything/
KeepEntryItems still loses its FiR tag. Set true to skip that stripping for raids this mod
is actively restoring gear for, so kept items stay flea-sellable as if you'd extracted with them.

NotifyPlayer (default true): sends an in-game system mail whenever this mod actively
restores gear - shows up as the normal SPT mail notification (popup + sound), with text
summarising the mode and how many items were kept. There's no client mod, so this - a mail
message via MailSendService.SendSystemMessageToPlayer - is the closest thing to a toast
notification a server-only mod can send. Set false to go back to silent.

release.html:
1. The app can now keep itself up to date.
  2. Endorsements feature added (this will require your cache to be re-run at startup)

It tells you when there's a new version

On launch it checks whether a newer version has been published and, if so, raises a banner and puts
a badge on the new App update item in the sidebar. That page shows what you're running, what's
been published, the release notes, and the button that installs it.

It tells you what kind of update it is, rather than leaving you to work out which of the three
numbers moved:

  • x.x.CHANGE - bug fix. Fixes to how the current version already works. Nothing new to learn,
    and safe to skip if nothing is broken for you.
  • x.CHANGE.x - feature update. Something new, or something works differently. Worth reading
    the notes.
  • CHANGE.x.x - major update. Significant changes. Read the notes and the mod page first.

The banner's colour follows the same split, so a bug fix doesn't announce itself the way a major
release does.

Closing the banner skips that release. It won't come back for that version - though anything
published after it will. The App update page is still there whenever you want it, with a
Check now button.

It still comes from sp-mod.com, the same as everything else

This app has its own mod page here, like any other mod you install through it. Nothing about this
feature works around sp-mod.com's processes and guidelines:

  • The check reads the public API, the same one Browse uses for every other mod.
  • The download is the file this mod page's own Download button serves - not a mirror, not
    GitHub, not a private channel.
  • You're asked to open the mod page before anything downloads, exactly as you are for every
    other mod in the app.

The only thing that changed about Browse is that the manager no longer lists itself among the
mods it installs - it isn't a mod, and installing it from there would drop a second copy into
BepInEx\plugins for SPT to try to load. It's still on the site, still browsable there, and the
update page links straight to it.

How the swap works

A running program can't overwrite itself, so this is done from outside it. The release is downloaded
and unpacked into a hidden .tcfmm-update\ folder next to the exe and checked over before anything
else happens. The app then starts a small script, closes, and the script waits for it to actually
exit before copying the new version into place and starting it again.

Nothing of yours is touched. The copy lays the new build over the old one and leaves the rest of
the folder exactly as it was - Data\ (your SPT path, install history, groups, caches), Staging\
and LegacyConfigs\ all carry straight over. There's nothing to migrate and nothing to back up
first.

If anything goes wrong, you keep the version you have. No write access to the folder, not enough
disk space, a copy that doesn't complete - in every case the working version is left alone and
restarted, and the unpacked new version stays in .tcfmm-update\payload\ so you can copy it over by
hand if you want it. What happened is written into the app's own log the next time it starts.

If the app is somewhere it can't write to - inside Program Files, say - it says so up front
instead of trying, and points you at the mod page.

Fixed

  • The title bar showed the wrong version. It had been reading v1.2.1-BETA since that release,
    regardless of what you actually had installed. It now reports the real one.

Browse: sort by endorsements

sp-mod.com added endorsements recently, and Browse can now sort by them — Most endorsed, in the
same Sort by dropdown as Most downloaded and Most favourited. Cards show the count too, on mods
that have any.

It's a new feature on the site, so the numbers are still small — the most endorsed mod in the whole
catalogue is in the low twenties, and most mods sit at zero. Past the first page or so, mods on the
same count are ordered by downloads, so the list stays useful rather than going arbitrary.

Worth knowing

  • This version has to be installed by hand - it's the one that adds self-updating, so there's
    nothing in your current copy that can fetch it. From v1.4.0-beta onward, updates can be done from
    inside the app.
  • The app is a single self-contained file with .NET and WPF bundled into it, so an update replaces
    the whole ~130MB of it rather than patching the parts that changed. It's one download either way,
    but don't be surprised by the size for a small fix.
  • Updating needs roughly four times the download size free on the drive the app is on, since the
    download and the unpacked build are both there at once. It checks first and tells you if not.
  • The app closing and reopening on its own is the update working, not a crash.
  • Only the manager updates itself this way. Your mods still update from the Installed page,
    exactly as before - nothing about that has changed.
  • The check runs once per launch, a few seconds in, so it doesn't compete with the catalog load. It
    failing - no connection, sp-mod.com rate limiting - is not an error; it just means no banner, and
    the App update page says why.
  • The first launch of this version re-pulls the mod catalogue once, so that endorsement counts are
    there for the new sort. Your first visit to Browse will be slower than usual; after that it's
    cached as before. Refresh cache on the Browse page does the same thing any time you want it.

Upgrading

Drop-in over v1.3.x. No settings, manifest or group-file changes, and nothing about existing
installs changes.

In this update, trader received error logs and, at your request, its own assortment configuration settings!

Now you can understand exactly what error the mod encountered (e.g., mod conflict or other errors). All logs are recorded in the server console (as well as in the .log file at SPT/user/logs/spt).

Now, about the config. It gives you convenient control over the merchant's assortment. Before you begin, you should understand that this config is server-side, which means it will be applied the next time the server is started. The config is created automatically when the server is first started in the directory SPT/user/mods/Tiltushkin-AllAmmo/config/.

You don't need to add anything to this config yourself. Each time the merchant's assortment changes, new items will be automatically added to the config. And if you suddenly add an item to the config that is not in the assortment, the mod will tell you about it and remove it from the config itself.

Next, about the configuration structure and possible settings:

“ID from assort (not tpl)”:
{
     “ItemName”: “string”,
     “PriceMultiplier”: 0.01 - infinity,
     “StockCount”: -1/0/your number
}

  • ID from assort - is the ID of the item from the merchant's assortment

  • ItemName - is the name of the item in the game (in English), you can change it to anything you want, it is done for convenience to understand what the item is

  • PriceMultiplier - is the multiplier of the base price of the item

  • StockCount - the number of item the merchant has. If you specify -1, the item will disappear from the merchant's assortment; if you specify 0, the standard number of items from the assortment will be used

release.html:
Tylevo's Tactical Services Control v1.0.8 Public Beta

Install-ready beta package for SPT 4.0.13. Extract it into the SPT root while the game and server are closed.

This update follows the published v1.0.7 build and contains the changes below.

Highlights

  • Support deployment now happens from the TSC Uplink phone. Buy an authorization, press the configurable deploy key, select the exact service you purchased, and designate the target without carrying the rangefinder.
  • The phone can automatically zoom and reframe itself while raised. Its default zoom FOV is now 45 for a slightly wider view; FOV and horizontal/vertical framing remain configurable in F12 and restore cleanly when the phone is stowed. Existing custom FOV values are preserved.
  • Purchase, deploy, and spotter-confirm keybinds are now visible in F12.
  • A-10 single and double passes stay separate from purchase through deployment, so selecting one no longer spends or launches the other.

Controls And Workflow

  • U (configurable in F12 as Open uplink key) opens the TSC Uplink in purchase mode.
  • On the purchase phone, press 1, 2, or 3 to open Extraction, Fire Support, or UAV Recon. Inside a category, 1 selects the standard service and 2 selects the upgraded variant when enabled. Press Enter on the confirmation screen to authorize payment. RMB returns to the previous screen; Escape closes the phone.
  • K (configurable in F12 as Open deploy key) opens the Uplink in deployment mode after you own an authorization. Only services you currently own are listed. Press 1-6 to select one, then LMB or Enter to deploy it. RMB, Backspace, or Escape stows the phone without spending anything.
  • A-10 and UH-60 use camera-based target designation after deployment; the rangefinder is no longer required. Press Mouse 2/middle mouse (configurable in F12 as Spotter confirm key) or Enter to confirm each targeting step. Alt+RMB or Backspace cancels targeting.
  • UAV Recon and Focused Sweep start directly after deployment and display the radar overlay only for the requesting player.

Payment And Authorizations

  • Fixed authorizations being duplicated, not consumed, or restored with the wrong service type.
  • Stash purchases are serialized and transactional. TSC restores the inventory if profile saving or authorization persistence fails, preventing lost roubles without a matching authorization.
  • PreferStashThenCarried now falls back to carried roubles when stash payment is unavailable.
  • The purchase endpoint accepts plain, zlib, and deflate request bodies and returns a controlled failure instead of crashing on malformed or unexpected input.
  • The authorization ledger now uses atomic saves, backups, corrupt-file preservation, and mutation rollback.

Fika And A-10

  • Exactly one raid-world authority executes an A-10 strike. Single-player and human Fika hosts retain the original Arys runtime/ballistic behavior; clients are visual-only.
  • Every support request carries a unique ID. In-flight and completed request gates prevent duplicate network packets from firing projectiles or consuming authorizations twice.
  • Fika clients wait for the host/headless acceptance broadcast before starting A-10 visuals.
  • Tracers and impact effects are aligned to the visible aircraft firing pass and keyed to the request, seed, and pass.
  • Dedicated-headless A-10 damage is available through the experimental headless executor and Fika damage packets. This remains intentionally gated and experimental.
  • UAV radar overlays are requester-local and are not created on a dedicated headless host.
  • Fika integration startup/shutdown and duplicate-request retention are bounded and safe across repeated raid initialization.

Stability And Compatibility

  • Fixed concurrent AssetBundle loading, including the UAV radar HUD double-load race.
  • Added compatibility with Manimal's HackerMod phone assets by reusing its complete phone bundle set when present.
  • Fixed null-reference teardown paths in SimpleSpinBlur, the fire-support pool, UI/controller cleanup, and phone camera restoration.
  • Hardened UH-60 extraction trigger cleanup and Fika extraction routing to reduce stuck black-screen exits.
  • Restored the loud A-10 strike flyover while keeping UAV loiter audio quiet and non-looping.

Updating

Extract over the existing installation. Back up SPT/user/mods/Tylevo.TacticalServicesControl/config/tsc-config.json first if it contains custom dashboard settings.

Required dependencies are not bundled: UnityToolkit v2.0.1, WTT Client Common Lib, and WTT Server Common Lib. Project Fika is optional and only required for multiplayer.

Known Issues

  • Remote third-person phone animation sync is not included.
  • Phone inventory inspect presentation may still need polish.

v2.0.1 — Hotfix

This patch addresses several bugs introduced in v2.0.0's hunter system and resolves a compatibility issue that prevented the mod from loading on some SPT 4.0.13 installs.

Bug Fixes

Hunter kill counter overflow
The hunter eliminated notification could display counts beyond the actual number of hunters (e.g. 7/2). PMC kills after all hunters were dead continued incrementing the counter. Both the counter and the hunter detection slot are now capped correctly.

Mod failing to load / TypeLoadException on raid start
In SPT 4.0.13, the EFT notification class is obfuscated to a non-standard Unicode character. Referencing it — or its nested enum types — by name caused a TypeLoadException at runtime that crashed the mod on raid entry. Notifications are now resolved entirely at runtime via reflection with no compile-time type references.

Bot spawning mod interference (ABPS / DONUTS / SWAG)
The hunter detection window was too wide (±60s), causing PMC waves from other bot spawning mods to be misidentified as hunters. The window is now tightened to ±15s around the fingerprinted spawn time (SpawnDelay + 0.1337s).

Hunter count hardcoded on client
The client was hardcoding hunter count and spawn chance values instead of reading from config.json. Changes to EscortCount, SpawnDelay, BaseChance, ChancePerSurvival, and MaxChance in the config now take effect without a recompile.

Changes

  • O key scan: Hunter status now shows Hunters in raid. or No hunters this raid. — kill count removed
  • Debug menu (F12): Added Force Hunters toggle to guarantee hunter spawns every raid for testing

Notes

The HunterStripPatch (which removes hunter spawns when the roll fails) is logging a warning on some installs — investigation ongoing. Hunters still function correctly when the roll succeeds. If you see Could not find BossLocationSpawn list in your BepInEx log, hunters may occasionally spawn even when the roll fails; this does not affect any other functionality.

A focused patch release fixing the biggest gripe with 1.2.0: zombies walking straight into trees, containers, and big props and getting stuck. They now properly navigate around obstacles, find routes through doorways, and pursue you across complex terrain.

Thanks to kobethuy who reported this specific enough feedback to diagnose in minutes.

What changed

  • Fixed: zombies now use EFT's NavMesh pathfinding properly. Previously we were inadvertently calling a direct-steer variant of BotOwner.GoToPoint that ignored NavMesh and walked bots in straight lines until something blocked them.
  • Internal: new diagnostic log at startup shows the resolved GoToPoint overload signature, making future API-drift bugs easy to spot.

What didn't change

  • Fast ("normal difficulty") zombies still chase from long range without respecting the pursuit-distance config. This was initially filed as a bug but — on reflection — running zombies that never give up is the mod working as intended. Relentless pursuit is a feature, not a bug.
  • Gameplay balance untouched: same horde sizes, same spawn chances, same melee/pistol mix as 1.2.0.

release.html: SPT Modern Weapon Mods (MWM) v1.0.0 release.

Major Update Changelog:

Manual Eating Interactions

  • Manual food eating! First step towards manual interactions, going to be implementing new interactions throughout this year
  • All foods now have unique gestures for manual eating, they're setup to be pretty intuitive and simple, tried to make it as seamless as possible where you barely need to think about it

Body Dragging

  • Added dragging AI bodies around (scavs will still loot the body at it's original location, I'll see if I can fix this)
  • Added dragging teammates body while it's in revive state when using Fika
  • To loot a body instead of drag, do a quick grip and let go

Full FIKA Sync

  • Synced arms over Fika, other players will now see where you're aiming
  • Synced manual eating
  • Synced body dragging
  • Synced loose loot holding
  • Synced melee hit effects
  • Created a separate Fika Sync .dll module so flatscreen players can install it and see the VR player movements too

Performance

  • Added lodbiasfactor slider in VR More settings (big performance boost when lowered but causes a lot of pop-in)
  • Fixed frustum culling for distant tree's, they won't disappear on the far right of vision anymore
  • Added option to change scope resolution in VR settings menu

Loose Loot Interaction

  • White dot will show up on items within a cone coming from the palm of your hand, the circle will grow/shrink based on another smaller raycast coming from your palm. So if multiple items are next to each other, you still have fine control over which item you select. Press grip from a distance when white dot is visible, it'll pull the item to your hand
  • Interact context menu now stays centered on where it is, even when the item it's connected to is moving
  • Context menu will only come up on items when you're holding and looking at it
  • Made it so joystick crouch/prone/jump is only blocked on context menus if the menu has more than one option to scroll to (makes use loose loot mod work, works perfectly with the manual eating) https://forge.sp-tarkov.com/mod/933/use-loose-loot
  • Fixed null when taking an item that you are currently holding
  • Made it so if you have loose loot use mod installed and use food/drink while holding the item, it'll put it in your inventory if there's space, if not, it'll drop the item and put you into eating/drinking state
  • Update to held item collision, if the collision causes the item to pull too far from your hand, it'll auto drop the item. There's some give to this so it wont just fall out of your hand with small bumps. For example, your hand will need to move about a foot away from whatever item your holding before it drops it
  • Significant improvement to held item stability, item gets parented to the hand. Little to no jitter at all while walking with item
  • Adjusted collision to use high poly collider instead of low poly for held items. This avoids mismatch of colliders when an item is dropped vs when you pick it up. This made clipping smaller items through stuff a lot harder
  • Held items will now be a lot harder to clip through collision, nearly impossible - when item meets collision, it'll slide along the collision to try and stay connected to your hand, it won't just get caught and stuck on collision anymore

VR Setting Menu

  • Smooth sliders for all VR slider settings so you can dial in exact offsets for things now, not limited to the ticks (all your current settings should be unchanged, the numbers in the settings menu are just different visibly to standardize and not just have a bunch of random numbers)
  • Scrollbar added to VR Settings menu - thanks killdns for the initial work on this, had to do a lot to get it working properly though in my headset and others
  • Added secondary VR settings menu called "VR More" which will be used for graphics and interaction related settings
  • Added disable mouse input toggle in VR More (fixes the issue where things get highlighted that your laser isn't pointing at when toggled)
  • Added walkeffector toggle in VR settings (this adds walking animation for guns/hands)
  • Added option to toggle corpse context menu

IK Improvements

  • Various improvements to IK/Jitter
  • Improved left hand rest pose when not two handing a gun
  • Shoulders no longer go lower than they should when crouching, this helps keep IK working consistently even when crouched. They always will stay 1-1 with head height
  • When crouching both physically and with joystick, your character will now move 1-1 with you. For example, if you look down then crouch really fast, you won't see your legs lagging behind
  • Fixed wrist twisting when running with disable run animation enabled (sometimes it starts twisting again I have no idea why, so not fully fixed yet)
  • Big improvement to overall stability when walking on uneven surfaces, this also significantly reduces that sudden jolt up/down when you start/stop walking while crouched

Variable Scope Rework

  • Total rework of variable scopes, it's all using base Tarkov's scope code now. I'm just taking full control of the FOV and making it analog. The result of this is that the scopes.json file is no longer needed and every scope should just work, even modded ones
  • Adjusted physical zoom dial to make the hand turn the direction you are actually turning your hand

UI Fixes

  • Edit build menu fully re-done, should work just like base eft now

Various Bug Fixes

  • Fixed sako and golden tt two handed grip
  • Laser pointer should now stay on loading screen all the way up until the countdown ends (only on fika, base spt is weird)
  • Fix to right click menu closing - no more stuck right click menu, if you click away from the menu, it'll close now as it should

Mod support

  • Added support for weapon customizer mod (moving attachments on rails, it all #justworks)
  • Added support for Loose Loot Use mod, works perfectly with the manual eating

Changes from the 0.10.3 Release:

  • Rewrote the server code for SPT 4.0
  • Moved client code to a new .NET Standard 2.1 project
  • Updated required version of SPT to 4.0.2
  • Updated required version of BigBrain to 1.4.0
  • Updated required version of Waypoints to 1.8.2
  • Made Phobos and ORBIT incompatible
  • Added support for Labyrinth:
    • Added Labyrinth quests (Fixes #90)
    • Added quests for the Labyrinth entrance on Shoreline
    • Bots will first try to complete quests to escape their starting chambers. After escaping, they will select random quests like normal.
    • With the Questing Bots spawning system, bot groups will be split up, and each member will spawn in its own starting chamber (like live EFT). Each member will try to escape its starting chamber before regrouping.
    • By default, all bots will be unable to pass through active traps in starting chambers. The traps must be disabled first.
    • By default, all bots will be unable to walk through the poison-tipped barbed wire placed throughout the map
    • By default, PMC and player Scav bots can set off the alarm when they reach the middle of the map
    • Added Labyrinth to various settings in config.json that are map-specific
    • Added Labyrinth-specific spawn-distance limits when using the Questing Bots spawning system
    • Added Labyrinth-specific distance threshold to the AI limiting system and allow AI limiting for questing bots on it
  • Added automatic detection of traps and alarm triggers (see #90 for more information)
  • Added new quest step types:
    • OpenNeabyDoors: Bots will open all doors within the specified radius of their starting point (currently bots cannot open locked doors)
    • Teleport: When bots reach the quest location, they will immediately teleport to the specified location
  • Added new quest features:
    • alarmQuest: Quests that can only be performed when the Labyrinth alarm is on
    • ignoreHearing: While performing the quest objective, bots will ignore footsteps and gunshots, unless they see an enemy or are hit by an enemy
    • prioritizeOverFollowing: If bots are instructed to perform a quest objective with this enabled, they will try to complete the objective without taking a break to regroup with their followers or boss (applies to both questing bots and questing boss followers).
    • forceUnlock: Forces bots to unlock all doors and toggle locked switches if necessary to complete the quest step
    • requireForFollowers: After completing the quest step, questing bosses will force their followers to perform the quest step too. They will wait until all followers complete (or fail) the step before proceeding.
  • Disable EFT's bot "local avoidance" system for questing bots (this caused erratic pathing behavior)
  • Increased the brain layer priority for AI limiting (sleeping) from 99 to 250 because the highest vanilla AI combat layer priority is 200.
  • Allow Labyrinth bot types, Cultist event bot types, Zryachiy event bot types, zombies, and Partisan to sleep and (if enabled in config.json) quest
  • Added F12 config option to allow custom bot types (added by other mods) to sleep (#106)
  • Added bot_spawns.player_scavs.disabled_maps config setting to prevent the Questing Bots spawning system from spawning player Scavs on specified maps even if DisabledForScav is changed to false for them by other mods
  • Prevent bots from trying to deactivate mines (grenade traps) unless they have a complete path to them
  • Improved pathfinding to switch positions when bots perform ToggleSwitch quest steps
  • Updated SAIN interop commands to make bots ignore gunfire sounds when forcing them to ignore hearing input
  • Prevent switches from returning to their initial states when bots interact with them (which sometimes happened on Labyrinth)
  • Raise CommandStatus.Begin and CommandStatus.Succeed events when bots interact with doors and switches
  • Added new interop methods (for #101):
    • GetCurrentQuestActionType(BotOwner bot)
    • GetCurrentQuestName(BotOwner bot)
    • GetCurrentQuestLocation(BotOwner bot)
    • IsCurrentJobAssignmentAnEftQuest(BotOwner bot)
    • HasAnActiveJobAssignment(BotOwner bot)
    • HasAQuestingBoss(BotOwner bot)
    • GetBotQuestInfo(BotOwner bot)
    • GetJobAssignmentHistory(BotOwner bot)
  • Improved performance of existing GetCurrentDecision(BotOwner bot) interop method
  • Added more overrides for EFT quest positions to improve bot questing accuracy
  • Updated server mods that automatically disable the Questing Bots spawning system (now only Acid's Bot Placement System and Unda)
  • Wait one frame before adding airdrop rush quest to ensure its NavMeshObstacle carves the NavMesh
  • Added override in config.json for SPT's player Scav brain-swap weightings (disabled by default; will require SPT 4.1 to work correctly)

Overview

Major Update - Happy New Year. This update introduces a full suite of experimental armor‑handling features centered around the Armband armor slot, along with expanded multi‑armor support, explosive redirection, and optional damage‑type suppression. The mod now provides a flexible, slot‑specific armor framework that integrates cleanly with EFT 0.16’s damage pipeline.

Update - Version support for SPT 4.0.0+ and EFT 0.16.9.0.40087

Update - License, Copyright, and versioning information.

New Features

  • Multi‑Layer Armor Damage Resolution (Experimental)
    • Ballistic armor damage can now be distributed across multiple worn armor pieces.
    • Armband armor participates fully in ballistic damage sharing.
    • Configurable toggle: Enable Multi-Layer Armor Damage Resolution.
  • Explosive Damage Redirection (Armband‑Only Experimental System)
    • Explosive damage can now be redirected away from the player and into armor durability.
    • Optional mode to redirect all explosive damage exclusively to the armband armor.
    • Configurable toggles:
    • Enable Protection From Explosives
    • Redirect All Explosive Damage to Armband Armor
  • Throughput Damage Suppression (Armband‑Only)
    • Prevents ballistic and explosive throughput damage from reaching the player.
    • Only applies when armband armor is equipped.
    • Configurable toggle: Disable Throughput Damage.
  • Blunt Damage Suppression (Armband‑Only)
    • Blocks all blunt trauma damage that would normally bypass armor.
    • Only applies when armband armor is equipped.
    • Configurable toggle: Disable Blunt Damage.
  • Fragmentation Damage Suppression (Armband‑Only)
    • Blocks grenade fragmentation damage from reaching the player.

release.html:
Bug fix release. Update if you are on 3.0.0 or 3.0.1.

Both fixes here came from player reports on the Forge. Keep them coming — they work.

Quest rewards crashed on redeem

Collecting the reward of a weapon quest threw "object reference not set to an instance of an object". The weapons handed out as rewards were missing required parts — a receiver, a barrel, a stock — so the game had nothing to build the item from at the moment it appeared in your inventory. Armour and helmets given as rewards had the same gap, without the crash: they simply arrived with no plates in them.

676 empty required slots across weapon_proficiency, weapon_mastery, iron_head, juggernaut and deep_pockets. All filled now, from the game's own default plates and factory presets.

Quests asking for a weapon, helmet or armour could not be handed in

Every handover condition in the mod carried a durability ceiling of 0. That field is an upper bound — 0 means "only accept an item with no durability left", so the game refused to let you drop any repairable item into the quest slot. Vanilla quests use 100, without exception. 3423 conditions corrected.

This one is inherited straight from the original 3.7.6 mod, not introduced by the port.

Nothing else changed

Quests, traders and bundles are identical to 3.0.1. Your progression carries over and no wipe is needed.

Install

Extract AndrudisQuestManiac-3.0.2-SPT4.1.zip into your SPT folder — the one containing EscapeFromTarkov.exe. Overwrite when asked. The mod lands in SPT_Runtime/user/mods/AndrudisQuestManiac/ on its own.

Requires WTT-CommonLib (the SPT 4.1 build). Kaeno-TraderScrolling is strongly recommended.

SPT 4.1 support

The plugin now works on SPT 4.0.x and 4.1.x from a single source tree.

SPT 4.1 ships a de-obfuscated EFT client in which several internal types were
renamed. Rather than track those names, the patch resolves everything it needs
by structure: it looks for a field whose type exposes the right shape, not
for a class called X. The plugin holds no compile-time reference to any game
assembly — only BepInEx, Harmony and two Unity modules. Each zip is
nonetheless built against its own SPT install, so you always get the binary
compiled for your branch.

If a future update breaks that resolution, the mod logs the failure and
disables itself. It never breaks your raid.

Project Fika (co-op)

Fika replaces the vanilla end-of-raid timer with its own, so earlier versions
simply never fired in co-op. The plugin now patches Fika's timer as well, as a
soft dependency: it is detected at runtime, and everything behaves exactly
as before when Fika is absent.

Fika support is new and lightly tested — please report anything odd.

Missing In Action on death

Dying in the gas sets your PMC to MIA rather than a plain death — he isn't
dead, he's lost in the gas. Switch it off in F12 for a normal death.

SPT 4.1 support, plus the grenade now counts for every grenade kill quest instead of just Grenadier. This release requires SPT 4.1.x — 2.0.3 will not load on it, and this build will not load on 4.0.x.

Install

Extract the archive over your SPT install root. Note that SPT 4.1 renamed the server folder, so the mod now lives in SPT_Runtime/user/mods/PineappleBlitz-LumurkFox rather than SPT/user/mods/.

The grenade keeps its item ID, so existing profiles that already own one are unaffected.

Quest support

Kills now count towards all three grenade quests:

  • Grenadier (Prapor)
  • The Art of Explosion (Prapor)
  • Fearless Beast (Jaeger)

Previously only Grenadier worked, because the quest and condition IDs were hardcoded. That approach turned out to be unsafe: Grenadier and The Art of Explosion share the same condition ID, and Fearless Beast whitelists only the event F-1 rather than the base F-1 this grenade is cloned from.

The mod now scans every quest at load and adds the grenade to any kill condition whose weapon whitelist already accepts a hand grenade. That covers all three today and automatically picks up any grenade quest added later, including ones added by other mods.

What changed

Ported to the 4.1 mod API. The server moved to .NET 10 and reworked how mods reach the database:

  • AbstractModMetadata was replaced by the IModMetadata interface
  • IOnLoad.OnLoad() became OnLoadAsync(CancellationToken)
  • DatabaseService.GetTables() was removed; tables and configs are injected directly
  • CustomItemService moved namespace and now takes the calling assembly

Because 4.1's database models are strongly typed, the entire reflection layer this mod relied on is gone — grenade properties, the Prapor barter and the bot blacklists are all set directly. Errors are logged instead of being silently swallowed.

BlacklistFromBots previously also added the grenade to the global item blacklist, which would have pulled it off the flea entirely and contradicted its own Prapor offer. It now uses the PMC loot blacklists and the lootable-item blacklist, keeping the grenade out of generated bot loot while leaving it purchasable and sellable.

commit.message: Add debug logging for file synchronization and configuration loading

release.html:
In version 1.0.2, there was a race condition, fix described below:

  • The code that processes files in parallel was previously using a HashSet to collect results.
  • HashSet<T> is not thread-safe: when multiple threads add items at the same time, it can corrupt internal state or throw exceptions.
  • That collection has been replaced with a ConcurrentBag<T>, which is specifically designed for concurrent writes from multiple threads without additional locking.

In practical terms:

  • Before: parallel file-processing tasks were all writing into a shared HashSet, risking intermittent crashes, missing entries, or corrupted data under load.
  • After: the same work is still done in parallel, but results go into a ConcurrentBag, so each thread can safely add items without stepping on each other.

So the race condition was resolved by switching to a thread-safe collection for shared parallel file processing, ensuring deterministic and stable behavior during synchronization.
